items.title: 台灣地方選舉：四成「陸配」參選遭剔除，「法理死結」如何困住參政之路？
items.description: 「除籍滿10年」如何計算，成為這屆選舉多位陸配被剔除參選資格的爭議焦點。今年有25位「陸配」參選，當中逾4成參選人不符參選資格。
items.content:
台灣地方選舉：四成「陸配」參選遭剔除，身分「法理死結」如何困住參政之路？
  - Author, 潘柏林
  - Role, BBC中文特約記者
  - Reporting from, 台北
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 4 分鐘
台灣下月舉行「九合一」地方選舉，今年有25位「陸配」參選，當中逾4成參選人不符「除籍滿10年」的參選資格，令參選人數減少至14人，較上屆19位參選陸配更少。
參選竹北市市長的前民眾黨立委李貞秀，是其中一位不符資格的陸配，她向法院聲請保留參選資格，法官在10月22日駁回聲請，但同時表明相關議題尚須經繁瑣的證據調查，為後續法律爭議留下懸念。
「除籍滿10年」如何計算，成為這屆選舉多位陸配被剔除參選資格的爭議焦點。BBC中文核對各縣市選委會官網資料，新竹縣以外，台北市、台中市和花蓮縣都有陸配不符「除籍10年」的例子。
有學者分析，陸配參選門檻隨兩岸情勢和台灣政黨輪替變化，本屆選舉民進黨政府採取嚴格審查，打擊陸配參與公共事務和從政的意願，讓陸配群體更多只在台灣過「社會生活」。
法庭裁決仍留下懸念
「陸配」是台灣普遍對中國大陸籍配偶的簡稱，近年也被稱為「中配」或「中國婚姻移民」。目前近37萬名陸配在台灣，其中約14.8萬人已取得中華民國身份證。
李貞秀因不獲批參選竹北市市長，早前向台北高等行政法院提出聲請，要求保留參選資格。
法院在10月22日駁回聲請，法官指李貞秀於1999年12月首次在台灣設立戶籍，至2025年3月才補繳大陸戶籍註銷證明，因為除籍未滿10年，被取消參選資格，形容「以現有事證，於法尚有據」。至於陸委會是否增加法律所無之限制，以及原處分是否違反比例原則等，法官認為尚須經過繁瑣的調查程序。
李貞秀對裁決深感遺憾，決定放棄抗告。她強調法律不應因人而異，不能因為無法選擇的出生背景，將特定族群當成二等公民。
台灣律師莊秀銘曾擔任地方法院法官，他向BBC中文表示，李貞秀聲請保留參選資格，是屬於處理緊急狀態的訴訟，聲請人必須有十分明顯證據說服法官，才會獲批。
台灣政治大學法學院副教授林佳和向BBC中文表示，這次裁決「暫時先避開」《國籍法》的爭論，相關爭議的法律訴訟空間依舊，包括行政訴訟、最高行政法院的上訴審，日後亦可能變成憲法爭議，進入憲法訴訟。
四成陸配被剔除、涉及多個縣市
李貞秀不是唯一被取消參選資格的陸配。
台灣陸委會副主委梁文傑在10月1日表示，經初步查證，今年25位參選的陸配，有4人沒有繳交喪失中國大陸戶籍證明；另外有7人有繳交證明，但除籍未滿10年。
換言之，本屆選舉多達4成陸配參選人不符合資格。
台灣中央選舉委員會回覆BBC中文查詢，確認九合一選舉有11位陸配不符候選人資格，當中包括參選直轄市議員1人、鄉鎮市長1人、村里長9人。另外14位陸配已繳附喪失原籍證明滿10年，符合參選資格，包括參選縣議員2人、鄉鎮市民代表2人、村里長10人。
資料顯示，上屆九合一選舉共有19位陸配參選，本屆則僅有14人符合資格，減少了5人。
目前已知台北市議員參選人游智彬、花蓮縣富里鄉學田村村長參選人賴汶佑、台中和台北各有一名里長參選人，均因為提交除籍證明未滿10年，無法登記參選。
國台辦發言人張晗今年7月回應陸配參選爭議，她指出大陸和台灣同屬一個中國，兩岸同胞是一家人，根本不存在所謂「國籍」問題，批評民進黨肆意打壓欺凌陸配群體，變本加厲限縮他們在台灣的參政權利。
梁文傑在10月22日稱，曾在中國設籍的人士，來台後沒有完成身分轉換的必備程序，「是他們沒有取得（參選）資格，不是我們把他的資格取消，這個是有差別的」。
國立台北大學公共行政暨政策學系劉嘉薇教授向BBC中文表示，執政民進黨在兩岸政策採取抗中保台態度，影響對陸配參選標準漸趨嚴格，「即使她已經成為台灣人的配偶，還是比較不相信她們能夠去保衛台灣的國家安全。」
陸委會核釋：「除籍滿十年」成參選門檻
陸配參選資格爭議，源於各方對《台灣地區與大陸地區人民關係條例》（簡稱兩岸條例）第21條的詮釋差異。
根據《兩岸條例》第21條，以往大陸地區人民「在台灣地區設有戶籍滿十年」，便可以登記為公職候選人。
到今年4月，陸委會發佈解釋令函，核釋《兩岸條例》第21條，指出中國大陸人民申請定居，未向主管機關提出喪失原籍證明文件前，因尚兼具中國大陸人民身分，無從解釋其已完成兩岸身分轉換，「在身分轉換過渡期間，依法無從主張已具有完整且穩定之台灣人民身分並享有相關權利」。
隨後中選會在7月宣布，陸配未來若申請登記為候選人，要繳交「喪失原籍證明」滿十年，才符合「在台灣設籍滿10年」的參選資格。當時中選會主委游盈隆強調，這是單純的行政作業程序，「沒有什麼這些複雜的政治考量在裡面」。
對部分已在台設籍多年，但尚未取消中國戶籍滿10年的陸配，根據最新核釋便不符參選資格，例如李貞秀於2024年立委選舉前後，仍持有中國大陸戶籍，直至2025年3月才補繳「喪失原籍證明」。
法律學者林佳和指出，陸籍參選爭議關鍵，在於台灣政府如何認定大陸地區人民的國籍及法律身分。
他表示，《兩岸人民關係條例》最早的立法思路，一方面不承認中華人民共和國存在，將大陸地區人民視為特殊的「本國人」，立法者加上特殊要件，要求大陸地區人民在台設籍滿10年，才可參選公職。
但蔡英文在執政最後一年，行政院在2023年5月通令各部會，停止適用或不再援用「大陸地區人民亦為中華民國人民」等相關函釋，並指出中國大陸人民不具中華民國國籍。
林佳和指出，賴清德政府進一步延續這一立場，包括透過核釋《兩岸條例》第21條，要求當事人繳交喪失中國大陸戶籍證明後，才開始計算參選所需的「在台設籍10年」年限。
政治學者劉嘉薇認為，在嚴格審查下，實際效果是降低陸配的參選意願。「他（陸配）好像只能在台灣過一種社會的生活，可是政治的生活，是沒有辦法去參選的。對於他融入台灣社會，其實是會有影響。」
放棄中國國籍，為何成難題？
陸配除了在參選時要符合放棄中國戶籍滿10年條件，當選後一年內亦要放棄中國國籍。
根據台灣《國籍法》第20條第4項規定，中華民國國民兼具「外國國籍」者，擬任公職時應於就職前辦理放棄外國國籍，並於就職之日起一年內，完成喪失該國國籍及取得證明文件。若屆期未完成，應予免職。
台灣內政部在2026年4月1日重申，原中國大陸人民取得台灣身分後，當選公職仍須遵守《國籍法》第20條，意味陸配需放棄中國國籍。
不過，陸配實際要放棄國籍難度極高。中國大陸法律規定，必須定居外國才能申請放棄國籍，在當下兩岸形勢下，北京當局並不視台灣為一個「國家」。
前花蓮縣富里鄉學田村村長鄧萬華，因未放棄中國國籍，去年8月遭富里鄉公所解除職務，成為全台首位因國籍問題被解職的陸配村里長。鄧萬華表示，曾請在中國的家人幫忙詢問放棄國籍，結果被任職公安局的同學臭罵了一通。
台灣中研院法律學研究所研究員蘇彥圖曾對BBC中文指出，「中國絕對不承認台灣是一個國家，不可能因為你已經移民到台灣，就允許你放棄國籍。」
學者林佳和指出，陸配即便放棄中國國籍，也引起不少國安疑慮，例如有人主張應剝奪或一定期間限制其狹義的公民權，包括選舉權或被選舉權。他不完全贊同有關主張，「因為這是個重要的人權議題，不應該一概而論地對陸配有比一般外國人歸化後更加嚴格的限制。」
林佳和認為，應在國家安全的脈絡下，依據個案具體情況去處理，而非過度形式主義的以期間長短來決定其權利。

items.title: 「英國政府對華政策摸著石頭過河」——國會報告
items.description: 下議院商業、創新、科學與貿易委員會的一份報告指出，英國政府對華事務的決策過程持續地「前後矛盾」。
items.content:
「英國政府對華政策摸著石頭過河」——國會報告
  - Author, 凱特·瓦內爾（Kate Whannel）
  - Role, BBC政治記者
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
英國國會下議院商業委員會的議員批評，英國政府未能兌現其承諾，對中國採取一致的政策方針，反而在決策上「見步行步」。
該委員會在其報告中表示，決策過程一直帶有「前後矛盾」的特徵，而此舉正在加劇國家安全風險。
委員會呼籲內閣大臣們阻止敏感數據轉移至中國，為企業與這個超級大國進行貿易提供明確規則，並禁止進口使用強迫勞動製造的產品。
英國商業部不同意報告的結論，並補充稱：「我們對中國的方針是一貫的，我們將在能夠合作的領域合作，並在必須挑戰的地方提出挑戰。」
「我們已將雙邊關係建立在更穩定、更平衡、更長遠的基礎上，並以清醒評估機遇與風險為依據。
「我們的貿易戰略明確指出，我們將把握一切機會推動經濟增長，同時絕不在國家安全問題上妥協；而我們與中國增加接觸，也使我們能在出現問題時直接提出關切。」
前首相施紀賢爵士（Sir Keir Starmer）曾尋求與中國建立更緊密的關係，認為英國無法忽視經濟機遇，同時堅稱這不應意味著在國家安全問題上作出妥協。
然而，一些關注中國涉嫌在英國從事間諜活動的議員批評建立雙邊關係的努力。
兩國關係審查已於去年完成，但政府表示文件包含機密資訊，因此尚未全文公開。
施紀賢的繼任者貝安德（Andy Burnham）至今尚未闡明其對英中關係的立場。
下議院商業、創新、科學及貿易委員會在報告中表示，歷屆政府都「未能讓公眾相信」，它們已採取「充分措施捍衛英國國家安全及經濟韌性」。
議員們表示，政府方針難以預測，加上缺乏明確指引，阻礙了企業與中國開展貿易的能力。
委員會建議設立「紅區」和「綠區」，明確界定哪些貿易與投資領域將受到鼓勵，以及哪些領域屬於「禁區」。
委員會表示，政府應堅持與中國進行公平貿易，並建議預先制定關稅措施，以便在中國繼續補貼本國產業，或未能提供「完全對等」市場准入時實施。
在保護敏感技術和數據方面，報告指出，應禁止在關鍵國家基礎設施中使用具連網功能的科技設備。
委員會表示，中國製造的「低成本」連網科技設備已在英國廣泛使用，而在這個領域，政府「將外交禮貌置於英國國家安全之上」。
報告還表示，大學在與中國機構開展研究合作時，應更快獲得相關建議。
委員會主席、執政工黨議員白理安（Liam Byrne）表示：「當政府一邊前進、一邊制定對華政策時，英國企業無法為未來作出規劃。」
「大臣們承諾提供清晰度和一致性。然而，我們看到的是機遇被錯失、風險未受管理，以及決定被拖到最後一刻才作出。」
「英國必須塑造自身與中國的關係，否則就有可能讓這段關係由華盛頓或北京替我們決定。」
本文原以英文撰寫，我們使用了人工智能協助翻譯，並由BBC記者在發佈前進行審核。了解更多關於我們如何使用人工智能的資訊。

items.title: 美國中期選舉：民調顯示民主黨將取得勝利，但預測還準確嗎？
items.description: 民調一直預測民主黨將取得大勝，但由於選民最後一刻的決定以及抽樣抽樣問題，最終結果無法保證。
items.content:
美國中期選舉：民調顯示民主黨將取得勝利，但預測還準確嗎？
  - Author, 安東尼·澤克爾（Anthony Zurcher）
  - Role, 駐北美記者
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
民主黨帶著很高的期望迎接這場舉足輕重的美國中期選舉。
一位支持率創歷史新低的共和黨總統、對食品和各項帳單費用上漲心懷不滿的美國公眾，以及連續數月對民主黨有利的民調，都預示著週二對民主黨而言將是個美好的夜晚。
民調顯示，民主黨候選人在遠超218個議席的選區中領先，而218席正是奪取國會下院眾議院（House of Representatives）控制權所需的席位數。在關鍵的參議院（Senate）選戰中，他們與對手持平或略微領先。
《紐約時報》（New York Times）近期的一項民調顯示，南卡羅來納州（South Carolina）的參議院選戰呈現平局，而唐納德·特朗普（Donald Trump）2024 年在該州領先18個百分點。有線電視新聞網（CNN）近期的調查則顯示，民主黨在得克薩斯州（Texas）、堪薩斯州（Kansas）和緬因州（Maine）領先。
但這些民調準確嗎？
美國近年的政治史上，民意調查失準的例子比比皆是，即便是在選舉前幾天進行的民調也不例外。特朗普在2016年和2024年入主白宮的過程中，表現都超出預測。2020 年，他以微弱差距落敗，而當時多數調查顯示民主黨人喬·拜登（Joe Biden）將更輕鬆獲勝。
今年早些時候，民調顯示民主黨人阿卜杜勒·埃爾-賽義德（Abdul El-Sayed）有望在密歇根州（Michigan）民主黨參議員初選中以兩位數優勢獲勝。結果差距僅為1%。在威斯康星州（Wisconsin）民主黨州長初選中，一名民調領先幅度接近20個百分點的候選人，最終以不到一個百分點的差距敗北。
進行政治和市場研究調查的益普索公共事務部（Ipsos Public Affairs）總裁克利福德·揚（Clifford Young）表示，近年來民調變得困難，原因是美國人紛紛棄用座機並過濾來電，聯繫他們更加不易。而且，民調機構聯繫到的人當中，許多人參與的意願也有所下降。
「保守派，尤其是極右翼保守派，本質上更加反建制，」揚說。 「他們什麼都不參與。他們憎恨這個體制。這就是挑戰所在。」
如果共和黨選民被系統性地低估，而民調公司在建立投票模型時沒有考慮到這一點，那麼他們的數據可能會向民主黨傾斜。
這也是民調機構越來越難以預測選民組成的原因之一。
特朗普在此前總統選舉中表現超出預期，一種解釋是，他的支持者——其中許多人並非經常投票的選民——以高於預期的人數湧向投票站。
這種不可預測性是近年來幾次明顯的民調失準的主要原因之一，儘管大多數信譽良好的民調的誤差只有幾個百分點。
在勢均力敵的選戰中，這幾個百分點就可能決定候選人的勝負。而今年，許多關鍵的參議院選戰都處於這樣狹窄的差距之內。
近年來，中期選舉的大選民調已被證明更為準確，部分原因是特朗普——以及他吸引心懷不滿的美國人前往投票的獨特能力——不在選票上。
2022年，民調顯示，儘管拜登的支持率低迷，民主黨仍將打破常規預期，避免遭遇選舉慘敗。
雖然民主黨最終失去了眾議院的控制權，但差距很小，而且民主黨保住了美國參議院的控制權。
雖然今年的初選結果確實帶來了更大的意外，但揚表示，初選歷來變數較大，選民更可能在最後一刻才做出決定。不應將此視為當前這批大選民調失準的跡象。
總統所在政黨在中期選舉中遭遇慘敗是很常見的。
近年來最引人注目的例子之一發生在 2010 年，當時共和黨人從民主黨手中奪得 60 多個眾議院席位，並在參議院也取得了進展。
那次選舉的背景是，經濟仍在從金融危機中艱難復甦，以及保守派對總統巴拉克·奧巴馬（Barack Obama）醫療改革的擔憂。民調曾預測民主黨會失利，但沒有預料到規模如此之大。
這次角色互換，民主黨成為反對黨，經濟議題成為選民關注的焦點。但鑑於特朗普的低支持率，民主黨的表現可能不會像歷史經驗所顯示的那樣好，也不會像一些人預期的那樣出色，原因有很多。
首先，這次選舉中涉及的大部分地區，特朗普在兩年前的總統選舉中都輕鬆拿下。對共和黨來說，這就像是主場比賽一樣。
其次，多年來眾議院選區邊界的調整，使得在兩黨之間易手的議席減少。
第三，由於國家的兩極分化加深，搖擺選民減少。一些專家形容選民群體已經僵化。
此外，共和黨一直享有資金優勢，這使他們在最後幾週有數億美元可用於投放攻擊性廣告。
民意調查模型旨在捕捉基本面的變化。精心設計的民意調查會預先考慮可能降低其可靠性的因素。
單一民調都存在固有的誤差範圍，這是基於樣本量與總體比例的統計不確定性。綜合來看，民調平均值而非單一調查結果可以提供更準確的預測。
目前來看，即使是像近幾屆總統選舉那樣的民調傾向，也顯示民主黨在11月3日晚上可能會取得不錯的成績。而且，民調失準可能偏向任何一方。在去年的州選舉和特別選舉中，民主黨的表現優於大多數民調預測，因為他們的選民投票率遠超預期。
特朗普在競選的最後幾天，在他2024年輕鬆獲勝的州舉行集會，這一景象提振了民主黨人的希望，他們認為共和黨內部民調顯示保守派候選人處境艱難。
不過，選民始終有可能直到選舉日當天都改變主意。
有時，後期的轉向會改變一場選戰的態勢。有時，未決定的選民——在許多此類選戰中他們仍佔選民的重要部分——會全部倒向同一方。
在民調中，總會存在一定程度的不確定性，而管理這種不確定性，正是與科學相伴的藝術。
「我認為我們做得更好了，」揚說。 「但我們一直面臨的問題不僅僅在於民調機構，部分原因在於我們正在和人打交道。人可不是那麼容易對付的。」

items.title: 美國對以色列的支持如何成為選舉爭議焦點
items.description: 對美國支持以色列的憂慮，如今正推動兩端立場的選民投票，成為美國中期選舉激烈選戰中的重要因素。
items.content:
「不是加沙，就是完蛋」：美國對以色列的支持如何成為選舉爭議焦點
  - Author, 阿斯瑪·哈立德（Asma Khalid）
  - Role, BBC國際部
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 5 分鐘
支持了民主黨大半輩子的薩姆拉·盧克曼（Samraa Luqman）自豪地投票支持唐納德·特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）連任美國總統。當時推動她投下這一票的，是單一議題，而這同樣將成為她在本週美國中期選舉中的投票考量。
這位也門裔美國人向BBC國際部電台節目《全球故事》（The Global Story, BBC World Service）表示：「不是加沙，就是完蛋。如果你在加沙、以色列和巴勒斯坦問題上的立場不好，我們不需要你在任，我們也不需要投票給你，不管你屬於哪個政黨。」
由於對美國支持以色列感到憤怒，像盧克曼這樣一向支持民主黨的選民，在2024年幫助共和黨在關鍵搖擺州密歇根州（Michigan；密西根）取得勝利。
類似的憂慮如今正推動爭議雙方的選民投票，成為11月選票上競爭最激烈的選戰之一中的重要因素。
密歇根州聯邦參議院空缺席位的激烈競爭，對於決定哪個政黨在特朗普餘下任期內控制國會至關重要。民主黨需要保住這個席位，共和黨則需要將其奪下。然而在選舉日到來之際，選情看來勢均力敵。
其中一方是民主黨人阿卜杜勒·埃爾—賽義德（Abdul El-Sayed）。這位醫生若在11月3日當選，將成為美國首位穆斯林聯邦參議員。
另一方則是共和黨人邁克·羅傑斯（Mike Rogers）。他曾是聯邦調查局（FBI）探員，並在眾議院任職14年。
儘管美國中期選舉通常圍繞經濟及生活成本等國內議題展開，但加沙戰爭幾乎已成為密歇根州選民的政治試金石。
基於不同原因，兩名候選人都強調美國在這場衝突上的支出。根據布朗大學（Brown University）「戰爭成本計劃」（Costs of War project）的數據，相關支出在首兩年已超過310億美元（1,397億元人民幣；6,860億元新台幣）。
獲特朗普支持的羅傑斯表示，美國向以色列提供軍事援助，以支持其在2023年10月7日哈馬斯主導襲擊後展開的軍事行動，關乎美國國家安全。
直言不諱的進步派人士埃爾—賽義德則多次譴責使用美國納稅人的金錢，資助他所形容的種族滅絕行為，而以色列強烈否認這項指控。
在密歇根州民主黨聯邦參議員候選人提名初選中，埃爾-賽義德以些微優勢擊敗立場溫和、堅定支持以色列的對手海莉·史蒂文斯（Haley Stevens）。
然而，就在星期二（11月3日）的投票開始前兩天，史蒂文斯公開表態支持羅傑斯，令民主黨同僚大感震驚。她形容兩人的對決是一場關乎「參議院良知」的戰鬥，也是對「仇恨」的一次公投。
在這場競選期間，外界批評雙方陣營充斥反穆斯林及反猶太攻擊；而史蒂文斯這一令人震驚的背書，則使原本持續發酵的意識形態緊張局勢徹底爆發。
密歇根州擁有全美最高比例的阿拉伯裔人口（Arab Americans），同時也有為數可觀、長期支持以色列的猶太選民。這兩個社群歷來都是民主黨的重要支持力量。
但到了2024年，情況出現變化。由於不滿民主黨在中東的外交政策，部分阿拉伯裔和穆斯林選民發起「不表態」（Uncommitted）運動，藉由拒絕表態支持任何候選人來表達不滿。
當總統候選人提名轉交給賀錦麗（Kamala Harris），而她承諾延續既有政策時，盧克曼等選民感到被背叛。
她說：「我非常憤怒，因為我大半輩子都只支持過民主黨。問題不只是他們沒有說出『停火』這個詞，或沒有試圖阻止種族滅絕，而是因為他們堅定地表示：『我們沒有做錯任何事，我們將繼續這些政策。』」
作為回應，盧克曼加入支持特朗普的穆斯林選民浪潮。她說：「我不只是投票給他，我還為他助選。」
不過，儘管她如今認為自己是共和黨人，盧克曼仍熱情支持埃爾—賽義德競選聯邦參議院席位。
另一名阿拉伯裔選民阿梅爾·扎哈爾（Amer Zahar）表示，民主黨是在經歷2024年選舉的警醒後，才開始接納像埃爾—賽義德這樣支持巴勒斯坦的候選人。
扎哈爾說：「民主黨並不總是代表我的聲音，我認為它也不總是代表我們社群的聲音。」
「我們必須在民主黨內發起一場革命，而這正是我們在2024年所做的事⋯⋯因此，在那場革命以及支持巴勒斯坦的候選人獲勝後，我們在那裏有了更多歸屬感。」
然而，儘管民主黨內部不斷變化的裂痕可能回應了不少阿拉伯裔選民的關切，另一群選民如今卻表達了被拋棄的憂慮。
有人質疑埃爾—賽義德在危機時刻保護猶太社群的能力。今年3月，以色列聖殿會堂（Temple Israel synagogue）遭到暴力襲擊後，他表示：「受傷的人會傷害別人。」襲擊者在以色列對黎巴嫩的一次空襲中失去了親屬。
埃爾—賽義德其後道歉，表示自己並非試圖為襲擊行為辯解，但此舉並未完全平息爭議。
密歇根州拉比委員會（Michigan Board of Rabbis）主席阿龍·斯塔爾（Aaron Starr）公開表示不會投票給埃爾—賽義德。他說：「那真的令人非常震驚。」
他對BBC《全球故事》表示：「我們社群中的大多數人一直投票支持民主黨，但現在卻感到民主黨一些成員的言論和行動，不是所有人，而是黨內某些候選人的言論和行動，正在危及我們的安全。」
就像2024年部分密歇根州穆斯林民主黨選民一樣，一些忠誠的猶太民主黨選民如今也正投票支持共和黨候選人，或者乾脆不投票。
律師兼密歇根大學（University of Michigan）校董喬丹·阿克爾（Jordan Acker）表示：「我是民主黨人，但首先我必須相信，我投票支持的人尊重我、尊重我的政治立場，以及我的存在。」
阿克爾已認識埃爾—賽義德20年。兩人曾一起上大學，但阿克爾不確定自己是否會投票給這位昔日同學。
他說：「在阿卜杜勒的世界觀裏，猶太人作為個體似乎是可以被接受的，但猶太人作為一個民族卻不可接受。對我而言，這非常令人不安。」
另一方面，羅傑斯一直試圖透過展現自己是以色列的堅定朋友來爭取該州猶太選民支持。他也曾稱埃爾—賽義德是「反猶人士」。
批評者指責羅傑斯透過將對手描繪成同情伊斯蘭極端主義的人來煽動對穆斯林的恐懼。羅傑斯和特朗普都曾指稱家族來自埃及的埃爾—賽義德與穆斯林兄弟會（Muslim Brotherhood）有聯繫。埃爾—賽義德則多次與該組織劃清界線，並否認任何關聯。
對相當一部分選民而言，這場激烈的參議院選戰不僅加劇了黨派分裂，也激化了種族與族裔緊張關係。不過，支持埃爾—賽義德的猶太選民大衛·弗羅因德（David Freund）並不太擔心長遠影響。
他說：「保障所有少數族群的安全，就是捍衛所有少數族群。猶太人的安全不會以一個名為『猶太人安全』的獨立類別被維護，它是關乎每個人民主權利這個更廣泛問題的一部分。」

items.title: 人工智能泡沫將爆破？這群「新雲端」公司正加劇市場擔憂
items.description: 這些數據中心正滾存著數百億英鎊的債務。
items.content:
人工智能泡沫將爆破？這群「新雲端」公司正加劇市場擔憂
  - Author, 莉莉·賈馬利（Lily Jamali）
  - Role, BBC北美科技記者
  - Reporting from, 舊金山（三藩市）報導
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI；人工智慧）生態系統中一個過去鮮為人知的領域，如今成為市場焦點，而投資者對其前景看法不一。
CoreWeave 和 Nebius 等公司名稱，對舊金山（三藩市）和硅谷（矽谷）的科技圈人士而言並不陌生。
這些數據中心公司被稱為「新雲端」（neocloud）企業，營運着大量擺滿昂貴電腦設備的數據中心，並將運算能力租賃給 Anthropic、OpenAI 及 Meta 等大型人工智能開發商。
如今，它們成為矽谷爭論最激烈話題之一。
不少人質疑新雲端（neocloud）企業的財務狀況是否穩健，以及它們近期遇到的挫折反映出人工智能經濟目前處於什麼狀態。
商業與科技研究機構「加特納」（Gartner）分析師預測，到2030年，80%的新雲端企業將「停止獨立營運」。另一方面，弗雷斯特研究公司（Forrester）專家則預期，至少有三家新雲端企業將在短期內被收購，因為其「財務狀況正變得不穩定」。
美國財政部長貝森特（Scott Bessent）上週四（10月29日）試圖淡化外界對新雲端企業的憂慮。他接受美國消費者新聞與商業頻道（CNBC）訪問時表示，這些公司只是「整體生態系統中的一小部分」。
債務擔憂
新雲端企業通常透過與需要快速取得運算能力的大型科技客戶簽訂長期租賃合約來融資。
首次公開招股（IPO）研究團隊「靜默期」（The Quiet Period）的分析師科里·約翰遜（Cory Johnson）解釋說，這些企業之後可利用相關合約，以及所購買的人工智能晶片作為抵押品借貸。
他指出，債務在新雲端企業中相當普遍，因為相關硬件設備需要預先支付成本。
以行業龍頭 CoreWeave 為例，其規模遠小於部分使用其服務的大型科技公司。
但約翰遜認為，放貸機構在提供貸款時，有時更看重 CoreWeave 客戶如微軟（Microsoft）和 Meta 的信用水平，而非 CoreWeave 本身的財務狀況。
他表示：「這有助解釋 CoreWeave 如何累積了351億美元（2,337億元人民幣；1.15兆元新台幣）債務。」
部分感到不安的投資者似乎開始改變看法。
過去一個月，CoreWeave 股價已下跌四分之一，而且並非個別例子。
其他新雲端企業，包括 Nebius、IREN 及 Applied Digital，同期股價跌幅亦大致相若，甚至更大。
債券投資者似乎也受到驚嚇，並開始要求行業內多家公司提供更高回報。
CoreWeave 行政總裁邁克·因特拉托（Mike Intrator）則表示，市場目前的反應是「非理性的」，並對公司的商業模式充滿信心。
全球一些最具影響力的企業正排隊使用 CoreWeave 的基建設施及其他人工智能服務。
起源於加密貨幣
部分新雲端企業源自劇烈波動的加密貨幣挖礦行業，這些公司生產比特幣等加密貨幣。
挖礦所需的基礎設施，與發展人工智能所需的設備有不少共通之處。
CoreWeave 於2017年成立，最初專注於以太坊（Ethereum）挖礦。
IREN、Core Scientific 及 Applied Digital 同樣以加密貨幣挖礦業務起家。
當 OpenAI 於2022年推出 ChatGPT，掀起人工智能熱潮時，這些公司原有的基礎設施令它們迅速取得優勢。
Nebius 則較為特殊。該公司前身為 Yandex NV，即被稱為「俄羅斯版谷歌（Google）」的 Yandex 母公司，並於2024年完成分拆及改名。
如今，這些企業的成敗很大程度取決於大型人工智能開發商，以及所謂的超大規模雲端服務商（hyperscalers）。後者是規模更龐大的數據中心營運商，而新雲端企業往往將其視為重要客戶。
標普全球（S&P Global）旗下「阿爾法洞察」（Visible Alpha）研究主管梅麗莎·奧托（Melissa Otto）表示：「目前有大量資金正源源不絕投入整個系統。」
「這是一場軍備競賽。」
而新雲端企業正是受惠者之一。
不過，弗雷斯特副總裁兼首席分析師查理·戴（Charlie Dai）表示，這種商業模式的代價是，一旦環境出現變化，企業將面臨「更高的財務風險」。
這包括大型科技客戶對支出計劃作出的任何調整。
就在過去一週，當微軟和谷歌預測未來人工智能投資規模低於華爾街分析師預期後，多家新雲端企業股價應聲下跌。
此外，市場亦高度關注 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的發展。兩家公司預計將於未來數月公開發售股份。
創投公司 Tusk Ventures 創辦人布拉德利·圖斯克（Bradley Tusk）表示，如果人工智能最終證明只是一場泡沫，而泡沫爆破的話：「新雲端企業肯定會受到連帶衝擊。」
「孔雀魚級的大規模死亡」
新雲端企業的未來，同樣取決於它們能否持續借貸，而當利率上升時，融資成本亦會隨之增加。
伊隆·馬斯克（Elon Musk）近日在社交平台發文表示，這項挑戰可能導致超過200家新雲端企業面臨「孔雀魚級別的死亡與合併」，當中規模最小的公司最為脆弱。
他補充說：「有些公司能夠撐過去，但不會太多。」
目前而言，Yorkville Ives 分析師表示，市場對運算能力的需求仍然超過供應，而新雲端企業正填補大型數據中心營運商無法滿足的重要缺口。
不過，在部分人士看來，新雲端產業近期的波動令人憂慮。
微軟近日因供電問題取消與英國新雲端企業 Nscale 的一項合作協議，而有關供電限制可能持續至2030年。
澳洲公司 Firmus 則剛剛擱置其 IPO 計劃。
這些發展出現在公眾對數據中心的反彈情緒升溫之際，市場亦開始質疑人工智能究竟能為員工生產力帶來多少實際價值。
約翰遜表示：「確實有理由感到擔憂。」

items.title: 德国总理呼吁朝韩统一 首尔愿意吗？
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德国总理呼吁朝韩统一-首尔愿意吗？/a-79832414?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 德国和朝鲜半岛一样，曾是一个因政治制度对立而分裂的国家，双方之间还隔着世界上设防最严密的边界之一。德国总理默茨近日访问韩国时表达了对朝鲜半岛实现统一的期待，但这样的愿望如今看来十分渺茫。
items.content:
德国总理呼吁朝韩统一 首尔愿意吗？
2026年11月2日
（德国之声中文网）朝鲜和韩国两个拥有共同历史、语言以及大量文化遗产，却彼此对立的国家，这故事在德国人听来并不陌生。
德国自己也曾在对立政权下分裂数十年，直到地缘政治局势发生变化，东西德才得以在1990年和平统一。
仅仅两年后，时任德国总理科尔（Helmut Kohl）访问朝鲜半岛非军事区（DMZ），表达了希望朝韩也能在本世纪90年代末实现统一的愿望。
但这一愿望最终未能实现。德国实现统一约35年后，朝韩依然在政治制度、经济发展以及地缘政治阵营上严重对立。
周五，德国总理默茨站在俯瞰朝鲜半岛非军事区的地方，所表达的愿望与科尔1993年提出的几乎如出一辙。
默茨在社交媒体上写道：“我们德国人知道国家分裂有多痛苦。我们也知道，只要坚守自己的价值观，并拥有对话的勇气，就有可能推倒高墙。”
默茨还表示：“我们祝愿朝鲜半岛人民能够在自由中实现统一。”
在长期关注朝韩政治动态的分析人士看来，这听起来更像是一个遥不可及的梦想。
韩国年轻人：统一？何必费这个劲?
朝鲜和韩国继续隔着非军事区相互戒备，双方在财富水平和政治自由方面的巨大差异也一览无余。
但最大的问题或许在于：朝韩双方似乎都没有表现出实现统一的意愿。
庆熙大学外交政策教授朱宰佑（Choo Jae-woo）表示：“过去二十年来，人们的心态已经发生了变化。在韩国年轻人眼中，朝鲜不过是邻近的一个国家，既贫穷又充满威胁。他们对朝鲜并没有像老一辈人那样怀有某种情感上的羁绊。”
他补充道：“越来越多的人在问，为什么还要费心去考虑统一的问题？”
首尔大学和平与统一研究所今年9月公布的一项调查显示，39.1%的韩国受访者认为统一已不可能实现。这是该调查开展约二十年以来的最高比例。
许多人担心，为朝鲜建设基础设施将耗费巨额资金，包括修建道路、医院和学校，以及现代社会正常运转所需的各项配套。
从官方立场来看，韩国政府并未放弃将国家统一作为目标。韩国宪法仍然主张以自由和民主为基础实现和平统一。但朱宰佑指出，近几届韩国政府对这一理念的宣传力度已经远不如过去。
朝鲜明确释放反对统一的信号
相比之下，朝鲜在这个问题上的立场则明确得多。
朱宰佑说：“2023年12月，金正恩宣布将修宪，和平统一已不再可能。相反，朝鲜将韩国视为敌对国家，且金正恩已无意推动双方走向统一。”
朝鲜修订后的宪法于2026年3月他通过。此后，金正恩政权更加激进，清除了宪法中所有关于和解及民族统一的表述。
首尔韩国外国语大学政治学与国际关系教授梅森·里奇（Mason Richey）表示：“我认为，朝鲜已经把话说得很明白了：它根本无意与韩国拉近关系。”
他补充说，每当朝鲜半岛统一问题再次被提起，韩国的分析人士、官员乃至普通民众都会开始“翻白眼”。
里奇指出，除了朝韩双方缺乏统一意愿之外，还有诸多其他挑战亟待克服。
朝鲜政权希望维护自身权力和威望。如果统一后的国家引入民主制度，朝鲜现政权的权力和地位必然受到威胁。
里奇表示，弥合朝韩之间巨大的经济发展差距将是一项艰巨工程，即使能够获得外部援助，也会给韩国带来巨大压力。
他指出，统一后的德国如今在大多数领域已经实现了东西部之间的平衡，但值得注意的是，1990年的东德发展水平仍远高于今天的朝鲜。
朝鲜半岛统一将给中美带来重大难题
根据韩国银行2024年的统计数据，朝鲜名义GDP每年为317亿美元，而韩国高达1.85万亿美元，是朝鲜的58倍。朝鲜人均GDP仅为1230美元，而韩国接近3.6万美元。
朱宰佑还指出，朝韩统一不仅是内部事务问题。两国在战略和安全领域分别依附于不同阵营：韩国与美国结盟，朝鲜则与中国保持紧密关系，并且越来越多地转向俄罗斯。
朱宰佑对德国之声表示：“这些大国不会愿意为了实现朝鲜半岛统一而放弃各自的盟友，因为统一对它们而言同样涉及重大的战略问题。美国不会希望出现一个倒向中国的统一朝鲜；如果统一意味着美国可能把军队部署到中国边境上、也就是今天的朝鲜境内,中国就会抵制统一。这是双方都无法想象的局面。”
他认为，归根结底，朝鲜半岛目前的现状或许并不完美，却是维持地区稳定的最佳方式。
不过，他补充说：“十年之后，经济、社会和安全局势可能会发生翻天覆地的变化。因此，我们永远不能把话说死。”

items.title: “Z世代”抗议活动引发暴力事件：“我们还必须审视根本原因”
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/z世代-抗议活动引发暴力事件：-我们还必须审视根本原因/a-79832382?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 上周六，德国各地有数万人举行了和平示威，但在美因河畔法兰克福，“Z世代”抗议活动后却发生了骚乱。汉堡、科隆、汉堡也出现暴力事件。德国政界就此展开讨论和反思。目前，欧洲多国学生和左翼社会组织联合发起了“国际青年罢工日”，并定于11月20日在全欧范围内举行大规模的罢工罢课。
items.content:
“Z世代”抗议活动引发暴力事件：“我们还必须审视根本原因”
2026年11月2日
（德国之声中文网）上周末“Z世代”抗议活动后法兰克福发生的暴力事件，持续在政治层面引发讨论。
德国内政部长亚历山大·多布林特（Alexander Dobrindt，基社盟）周日在接受《图片报》（Bild）在线版采访时表示：“左翼暴力团体和具有移民背景的滋事者绑架了当天早些时候进行的和平示威活动。我们将查明这些暴徒和抢劫者的身份，并追究其法律责任。这种破坏社会安宁的行为必须受到严厉惩处。”
有关移民群体的讨论
德国教育部长卡琳·普里恩（ Karin Prien，基民盟）认为，这些事件也引出了一个问题：如何才能更成功地实现社会融合。她在接受德意志电台（Deutschlandfunk）采访时提到，极左团体以及“可能具有移民背景的人群”参与了“过激的暴力行为”。她强调，这不是煽动怨恨，而是要探究为何有人会采取此类手段。“如果他们确实有移民背景，那我们必须关注，必须审视其背后的根本原因”，卡琳·普里恩说。她指出，一个关键问题是， 为何某些群体在社会融合方面不如其他群体。这位部长明确表示，她并不支持“Z世代”提出的所有诉求，比如在兵役问题上，但她主张对话，尤其是倾听那些未参与暴力活动的年轻人的心声。
法兰克福所在的黑森州州长鲍里斯·莱茵（Boris Rhein，基民盟）对法兰克福发生的暴力事件感到震惊。黑森州内政部长罗曼·波塞克（Roman Poseck，基民盟）表示，法兰克福骚乱的肇事者有两类，先是左翼极端分子，随后是“有移民背景的年轻人”加入。他在通报中称，被捕者年龄在13至29岁之间，“其中绝大多数是德国公民”。波塞克还指出：“我们有理由认为，肇事者中只有极少数来自法兰克福本地；许多人是从周边地区赶来的，还有一些人来自更远的地方。这些人绝大多数具有移民背景。“
德国国防部长皮斯托里乌斯（Boris Pistorius，社民党）不同意联盟党（基民盟/基社盟）政治家的解读。在接受德国电视二台（ZDF）采访时，他反问道：“所谓的‘移民群体’究竟是指什么？是指那些已经在德国生活了三代、且身为德国公民的人吗？我们到底要在什么时候才能停止这种区分？我认为，这会引向错误的方向。”
科隆警察局长约翰内斯·赫尔曼斯（Johannes Hermanns）表示：“令人痛心且深感不安的是，那些本意是为自身未来进行和平示威的年轻人，今天却被一些一心只想制造暴力的极端分子渗透了。”
社民党联邦议院党团呼吁召开全国教育峰会。该党团副主席施密特（Schmidt）指出，有权获得良好教育和职业培训的权利是此次示威活动的核心诉求之一。她主张德国发起一场由联邦、州和地方各级政府共同参与的教育峰会。
在周六晚间法兰克福的骚乱中，暴徒向安全部队投掷燃烧瓶和鞭炮，并砸碎了多家商店，包括一家枪支商店的橱窗。安全部队动用了水炮车、装甲车、直升机和无人机。大量人员被暂时拘留。超过100名警员在冲突中受伤。柏林、汉堡和科隆等德国其他城市也发生了暴力事件。德国内政部长多布林特对安全部队的表现给予了肯定。他表示：“多亏了我们尽职尽责的警员，才避免了像巴黎那样严重的暴力失控局面。警方保持大规模警力在场并分散部署的行动策略被证明是成功的。”
”Z世代做主”是一个什么组织？
此前号召在德国30多个城市举行和平示威的“Z世代做主”（Gen Z regelt）倡议组织的发言人表示，集会结束后所发生的一切，我们无法施加任何影响。该组织在Instagram上发文，明确与“任何形式的暴力，以及由非示威参与者的其他团体或个人所实施的暴力行为”划清界限。声明写道：“我们主张和平抗议、民主价值观以及自由表达意见的权利。暴力从来不是、也永远不会是我们运动的一部分。”
“Z世代做主”倡议组织提出的诉求包括增加学校经费、促进社会正义、采取措施应对不断上涨的生活成本，以及加强气候保护。这个由年轻人组成的松散联盟主要通过社交媒体进行协调，其具体组织架构及参与人员尚不明确。一个名叫阿克拉姆·塞洛（Akram Selo）的人被列为抗议活动的主要平台——“Z世代做主”网站的运营者。此人自称是一名18岁的高中生，其登记地址位于瑞士。他在接受《明星周刊》（Stern）采访时表示，这一倡议背后是一群“想要做出改变的年轻人”，通过TikTok建立联系。在接受《法兰克福汇报》（FAZ）采访时，塞洛称自己正在准备参加德国高中毕业考试，目前的组织团队由五人组成，其中三人选择保持匿名。他们居住在不同的城市，且并非所有成员彼此都相识。从《法兰克福汇报》的采访中可以看出，他对自己的人身安全感到担忧。
三周后的“国际青年罢工日”
该倡议组织计划在三周内再次在全国范围内动员大规模人群，并在“Z世代做主”的网站上呼吁人们为了教育、健康、气候保护，以及负担得起的生活，11月20日在34个德国城市参加全欧洲范围内抗议活动。
一个广泛的联盟号召人们参与11月20日的“国际青年罢工日”（International Youth Strike）。该联盟成员包括“联邦学生大会”（BSK）——此前，该组织曾与“Z世代做主”（Gen Z regelt）这一倡议活动保持距离。
（德新社、法新社、路透社）

items.title: 德语媒体：面对中美强权 中等强国应抱团取暖？
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：面对中美强权-中等强国应抱团取暖？/a-79831978?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 《商报》评论认为，德国总理默茨上周的亚洲之行发出了明确的信息：中等强国必须联合起来，才能应对大国施压。《法兰克福汇报》认为，默茨总理将对外经济合作列为施政要点，是一个非常明智的选择。
items.content:
（德国之声中文网）《商报》评论写道，无论是新加坡、东京，还是首尔，此次德国总理所到之处，似乎习近平和特朗普一直如影随形。因为每当默茨总理谈及自由贸易和经济依赖问题时，人们总是会联想到美国和中国。这篇题为《唯有携手盟友》的评论写道：
“对于联邦总统选举等德国内政事项，默茨总理的确有所怠慢，但对于全球力量格局的变化，他却非常的敏感。对于基社盟政治家艾格内尔（Ilse Aigner）是否应入主总统府的讨论，默茨作为总理显然没有予以足够的重视。但对于尽快给予特朗普、习近平和普京以明确回应，而不应委曲求全、矮化自己，默茨却有着非常清醒的认识。
事实上，就任总理之后，形势比人强，默茨的立场已经发生了变化。去年，默茨首次以德国总理身份访问华盛顿时，还曾对同特朗普开展合作充满信心。然而，一年半过后，这份信心几乎荡然无存。而同今年年初访华时的情景相比，现实也已经发生了很大的变化。总而言之，默茨对中美两国的措辞变得越来越强硬。柏林当然不希望发生贸易战，但也同样不能接受不公平的依赖关系。用来自柏林政治圈的话说就是，‘语气’已经变了，在对华政策问题上尤为如此。”
《商报》评论指出，敢于对中美两大强国“说不”，是默茨此次亚洲之行所发出的明确信号，而且也获得了盟友们的积极响应：
“不过，私下里也传出一些疑虑的声音。日本和韩国就很担心，德国和欧洲采取更为强硬的对华政策之后，会不会从整体上转向贸易保护主义，从而使日韩也陷入不利境地。默茨总理对这种担忧表示惊讶，也进行了必要的解释。但这也恰恰体现了此次亚洲之行的意义所在：只有通过密切的交流和沟通，才能发现彼此的顾虑和担忧，才能最终建立起经得起考验的伙伴关系。也只有这样，中等强国联盟战略才能充满活力。”
”出访亚洲是正确的选择“
内政危机不断加剧的关键时刻，总理默茨选择出访亚洲，因此在德国国内招致了“逃避现实”、“不务正业”的批评。《法兰克福汇报》评论写道：
“无论如何，默茨此次出行都是一个正确的决定。德国每四个工作岗位中，就有一个依赖出口，工业领域这一比例更是接近一半。中国咄咄逼人的贸易政策每个月都会导致德国流失1.5万个就业岗位。而与此同时，美国作为贸易伙伴也已不再靠谱。有鉴于此，德国经济急需同其他国家建立伙伴合作关系。德国总理亲自出马寻求伙伴，无疑是一件好事。
在德国，并不是所有人都意识到了‘中国冲击2.0’对德国繁荣构成了多么大的威胁。如果德国的经济前景得不到改善，后果将不堪设想。相比之下，工作45年后是否能拿到全额退休金，父母能休几个月的育儿假就都不是紧要问题了。在战争不断、危机四伏的当今世界，德国却仍在就如何捍卫社会福利制度而吵得不可开交，这简直让人感到不可思议。德国很少将对外贸易列为施政重点，而默茨正是通过此次亚洲之行，强调了对外贸易的重要性。
在基民盟内部，一些同经济界关系密切的人士对默茨总理的对华政策颇有微词。然而，当中国以补贴和压低汇率的方式冲击全球市场，将关键原材料当作地缘政治武器时，欧洲难道要袖手旁观吗？当然，欧洲人也不应矫枉过正，当前拟议中的‘欧洲制造’政策，同样也引起了默茨正在争取的东亚和东南亚国家的不满。除了各类强调友谊的宣言之外，这也是默茨此次带回柏林的重要信息。”

items.title: 美国中期选举周二登场：选什么？有哪些看点？
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/美国中期选举周二登场：选什么？有哪些看点？/a-79829479?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 美国于11月3日举行中期选举，选民将选出新一届国会众议员，并改选部分参议员，同时在多个州选出州长。这场选举不仅关系到国会两院的控制权，也被视为对总统特朗普及其执政表现的一次重要检验。民主党能否夺回国会控制权？哪些州和选区的选战最受关注？
items.content:
美国中期选举周二登场：选什么？有哪些看点？
2026年11月2日
（德国之声中文网）美国中期在本周二（11月3日）到来。美国选民决定的不是谁将入主白宫，而是谁将进入国会大厦。
中期选举每四年举行一次，时间恰好处于两次总统选举之间。美国有投票资格的选民将选出代表自己在国会两院，众议院和参议院任职的议员。此外，部分州还将举行州长选举。
不过，除了明确列出的这些具体人选外，选民实际上还会对另一件事作出评判。
美国弗吉尼亚大学政治中心（University of Virginia Center for Politics）选举分析师科尔曼（J. Miles Coleman）在2022年中期选举曾解释道，中期选举往往被视为“对总统及其执政党的一次公投”。如果民众对执政表现满意，总统所属政党的选情通常会更好；如果民众不满，该党表现则会更差。目前，美国总统特朗普的支持率已跌至历史低点。
中期选举选什么?
美国众议院全部席位都将改选。全美选民将投票选出435名拥有表决权的众议员，每名议员代表一个选区。选区划分主要依据人口分布情况。
因此，像怀俄明州这样人口较少的州，即使面积相对较大，也只有一个众议院席位。新泽西州的面积小得多，但人口更多，因此拥有12个席位。众议员每两年选举一次，任期也是两年。
美国参议员的任期则为六年，共100个席位，每个州无论人口多少，都拥有两个席位。每两年，约三分之一的参议院席位进行改选。今年的中期选举，选民将对其中35个席位进行投票。因此，与众议院选举不同，并非每个州都会在此次中期选举中改选参议员。
此外，美国36个州还将举行州长选举。州长任期通常为四年。
在美国，许多政策决定是在州一级作出的，涉及堕胎权、教育问题，乃至各类选举的组织和实施。因此，一个州由民主党还是共和党掌权，对当地居民的生活会产生重大影响。
目前美国国会由哪个党掌握多数？
目前，共和党，也就是特朗普总统所属的政党，在国会参众两院都占据多数，但领先优势并不大。
众议院目前有218名共和党议员、214名民主党议员，另有一名通常与共和党人投票立场一致的独立议员。还有两个席位空缺。
专家认为，民主党很可能在即将到来的选举中夺回众议院多数席位。科尔曼在10月底接受美国哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）采访时表示：“如果民主党连众议院都没能拿下，那才令人意外。”
参议院目前有53名共和党议员和45名民主党议员，以及两名通常与民主党投票立场一致的独立参议员。如果参议院表决出现50比50的平局，将由副总统投下决定性一票。因此，副总统、共和党人万斯是关键的一票。
为什么中期选举如此重要？
虽然中期选举的投票率通常低于总统选举，但选举结果同样会对未来数年的美国政治产生重大影响。
美国总统虽然拥有很大权力，可以通过行政命令（Executive Orders）直接作出一些决定，但许多政策措施仍须获得国会批准，否则便无法落实。
因此，如果共和党能在国会两院继续保持多数，特朗普贯彻自己的意图就会容易得多。果民主党夺得一院甚至两院的多数，特朗普要推行内政外交方面的改变就会更加困难。
哪些选战是胜负关键？
在众议院选举中，民主党只需净增四个席位，就能以218席的优势取得多数。在全部435场选区选举中，只有少数选区的胜负尚存悬念，其中包括爱荷华州、弗吉尼亚州和蒙大拿州的部分选区。
参议院选举中，得克萨斯州的选情尤其引人关注。根据最新民调，民主党候选人詹姆斯·塔拉里科（James Talarico）与共和党候选人肯·帕克斯顿（Ken Paxton）的支持率不相上下。
民主党若要在参议院取得多数，必须净增四个席位。得克萨斯州若成为其中一个席位，将是轰动性消息。自1994年以来，民主党候选人从未在该州赢得州级选举。
如今，塔拉里科甚至获得了诞生过两位美国总统、共和党政治世家-布什家族部分成员的支持。
州长选举方面，美国可能首次选出一位黑人女性州长。
在明尼苏达州，民主党人克洛布彻（Amy Klobuchar）与黑人共和党人德穆斯（Lisa DeMuth）角逐州长职位。在佐治亚州，黑人民主党人博顿斯（Keisha Lance Bottoms）也在竞选州长，她的对手是共和党人杰克逊（Rick Jackson）。
德穆斯在明尼苏达州胜出的可能性不大。该州通常被视为民主党占优势的州，而长期担任参议员的克洛布彻知名度也更高。
但在佐治亚州，根据最新民调，两名候选人的支持率十分接近。博顿斯有实实在在的胜选机会。

items.description: 阿曼国家元首自1978年中阿两国建交以来首次访华。中国国家主席习近平周一会见阿曼苏丹海赛姆时表示，中东和海湾地区不应成为大国博弈的角斗场，中方始终积极致力于止战促和。访问期间，中国和阿曼发表深化战略伙伴关系联合声明。
items.content:
建交后阿曼苏丹首次访华 习近平：中东不应成为大国博弈角斗场
2026年11月2日
（ 德国之声中文网）阿曼苏丹海赛姆周日晚抵达北京，开启对中国为期两天的国事访问。中国人民银行行长潘功胜作为中方高级官员代表前往机场接机，凸显中国与阿曼加强金融合作的意愿。此次访问是海赛姆继任苏丹以来首次访华，也是中阿两国建交48年来阿曼国家元首首次访问中国。
本周一（11月2日），中国国家主席习近平在北京人民大会堂同海赛姆举行会谈。习近平表示，当今世界正经历“百年未有之大变局”，中东海湾地区不应成为大国博弈和地缘冲突的角力场，中国愿与阿曼等国共同为早日恢复地区和平安宁而努力。习近平强调，中阿要增进政治互信，中方愿同阿方深化发展战略对接，推动能源，产业、投资、人工智能等合作。
上周，中国外交部表示，中方近期将派遣特使前往中东，旨在促进各方接触并推动局势降温。
据阿曼官方媒体报道，海赛姆向习近平表示，阿曼政府高度赞赏中方在涉及该地区重大问题上的立场。他说： “国家的繁荣需要一个以安全、和平、尊重国家主权及遵守国际法为特征的环境。争端应通过和平方式得到解决。” 他还表示，阿曼持开放态度，愿与中国商签双边贸易与投资优惠协定。
会谈后，习近平和海赛姆共同见证签署产供链、绿色发展、数字金融等领域多项合作文件。
深化战略伙伴关系
中国总理李强也同海赛姆苏丹举行会晤。两国之后发表关于深化战略伙伴关系的联合声明，其中包括双方同意深化共建“一带一路”倡议和阿曼“2040愿景”战略对接，加强双向投资合作，深化人工智能领域合作，在航天领域开展合作，以及“愿以签署本币互换协议为契机深化金融合作”。双方还强调推动尽早达成中国与海湾阿拉伯国家合作委员会的自由贸易协定。
此外，联合声明还强调，双方一致同意在涉及彼此核心利益和重大关切问题上继续相互支持，阿方支持习近平提出的构建人类命运共同体理念，以及高质量共建“一带一路”等重大倡议，双方坚定致力于维护以联合国为核心的国际体系，践行真正的多边主义，鼓励美国和伊朗坚持和平选择，尽早实现全面停火止战，“双方认为霍尔木兹海峡应恢复正常、安全通航，同意就海峡有关问题保持沟通”。声明还呼吁也门问题相关各方以也门人民利益为重，坚持通过对话协商化解分歧。长期遭受战乱困扰的也门是安曼的邻国。
中国是阿曼最大的贸易伙伴。阿曼是中国在阿拉伯国家中的第四大贸易伙伴。2025年双边贸易额为 328.7亿美元。中国主要从阿曼进口原油、液化天然气等，而中国向阿曼出口的产品主要为机电产品、钢铁、新能源装备及高新技术产品等。中国和阿曼2018年建立战略伙伴关系。自去年11月北京与马斯喀特之间开通直航以来，两国在旅游和商业领域的联系得到了进一步加强。
（路透社、新华社等）

Trump’s approval rating is near a career low ahead of elections, poll finds
A broad swathe of the US electorate see their vote in Tuesday’s midterms as a way to oppose the president, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll
US President Donald Trump’s approval rating held near a career low as a broad swathe of the US electorate saw their vote in Tuesday’s congressional midterm elections as a way to oppose the Republican president, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday.
The poll results underscore Republican vulnerabilities brought on by a surge in fuel prices since Trump launched a war on Iran in February. Voters in the nationwide poll said they preferred Democrats over Republicans - 46 per cent to 38 per cent - in what is known as a “generic ballot” question.
Still, that 8 percentage point Democratic advantage was narrower than in a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted a week earlier, when Democrats led by 11 points.

Netanyahu is pressing Trump to attack Iran after US midterm elections, officials say
Netanyahu is working with senior US figures to persuade Trump to launch a quick but extensive air campaign in Iran, an official said
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday’s midterm elections in the United States, according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter.
A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week’s elections. US President Donald Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes while pushing for a deal with Iran.
The two officials said diplomatic efforts have made progress, with Qatari mediators holding two rounds of talks last week with Iranian officials. The two officials said the mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to cease its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in return for the US lifting its blockade on Iran’s ports.

items.content:
US judge dismisses Trump administration’s Harvard race data admissions case
The judge agreed with Harvard that the Justice Department had not taken the necessary legal steps before suing the university
A federal judge on Monday dismissed a lawsuit by US President Donald Trump’s administration seeking to force Harvard University to turn over records for an investigation into whether it continues to consider race in its student admissions process.
US District Judge Myong Joun in Boston rejected the US Department of Justice’s lawsuit, which Harvard contends was filed as part of a broader campaign by the Republican president’s administration against the Ivy League school.
The judge stressed that his decision rested on narrow, procedural grounds and did not resolve whether the Justice Department and US Department of Education could ultimately seek data on thousands of high school students who sought admission at Harvard.

Long delays for Hong Kong court cases demand urgent action
The city’s drive to become a leading international centre for legal services depends on justice neither being denied nor delayed
3-MIN READ3-MIN
 Listen
A journalist for more than 30 years, Cliff Buddle began his career as a court reporter in London and moved to Hong Kong in 1994 to join the SCMP. 
Justice delayed, it is often said, is justice denied. If that is true, many court users in Hong Kong are being failed by the system.
Those involved in criminal cases at the Court of First Instance must wait 358 days on average for the hearing, the judiciary revealed last week. The figure for the District Court is 354 days, way above the court’s 100-day target. This is a cause of concern.
The glacial process has prompted the Law Society to call for drastic measures. Justin Yuen Hoi-ying, chairman of the body’s standing committee on standards and development, urged the judiciary to consider extending court hours. He suggested simple and procedural matters might be heard in the evenings or on Sundays.

items.title: Mahmood scraps settlement plans for migrant care workers
items.description: The home secretary laid out a revised proposal for changing when migrants can claim permanent residency.
items.content:
Mahmood scraps settlement plans for migrant care workers
- Published
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has scrapped plans to make foreign care workers already in the UK wait 15 years to qualify for permanent settlement.
Mahmood had proposed doubling the wait for indefinite leave to remain (ILR) from five years to 10 for most migrants, with some facing a 15-year wait.
But following a backlash from several Labour MPs, Mahmood revised the policy and care workers who earn at least £25,000 a year and arrived in the UK before May 2025 would continue to qualify after five years.
The Conservatives said Mahmood's "U-turn" would cost taxpayers billions of pounds.
ILR, also known as settlement, gives a person the right to live, work and study in the UK for as long as they like and apply for benefits if they are eligible. They can also use it to apply for British citizenship.
Last November, Mahmood announced plans to delay settlements in response to concerns over the number of people approaching eligibility, in the wake of record post-Brexit net migration figures under the previous Conservative government, nicknamed the "Boriswave".
Asked by the BBC whether she had u-turned on her earlier promises, she replied "I don't accept that", adding that some 500,000 people in the UK "will not now settle at five years".
"They will have to wait longer before they can achieve settlement in this country, and I've come to a fair resolution for care workers," she said.
The Home Office has said its figures show net migration - the difference between those entering and leaving the country - added 2.6m people to the UK population between 2021 and 2024.
The department estimates that between 2026 and 2030 between 1.3m and 2.2m people will settle in the UK, adding its central estimate has increased to 1.9m.
The home secretary faced criticism for proposing to apply the changes to migrant workers already in the UK, with Housing Secretary Angela Rayner previously saying this would "change the goalposts".
Several Labour MPs also described the retrospective approach as "un-British" and warned it could worsen the UK's skills shortage, particularly in the care sector.
Making a statement to the House of Commons, Mahmood said settlement "should not be automatic, it should be earned".
- Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes 
  - Published1 hour ago
- What are the planned changes to immigration rules? 
  - Published4 hours ago
The changes will move those earning less than £50,000 a year onto a 10-year path to settlement status, unless they are exempt.
Mahmood also told MPs the government would provide a five-year path to settlement for care workers who "answered our call when we needed them" following the Covid-19 pandemic.
Mahmood said: "Those who earn £25,000 a year working in the social care sector, which was the condition of their visa, will therefore be able to settle on their existing five-year path."
She added those care workers who did not meet the conditions of their visa could apply for another five-year visa and seek settlement after that.
MPs were also told:
- higher earners on salaries of more than £50,000 and those who have contributed in healthcare and education, such as doctors and teachers, will be able to qualify for settlement after five years
- the highest rate taxpayers earning more than £125,000 will be able to apply after three years
- refugees who arrived in the UK after crossing the Channel by small boat or another illegal route will have to wait 20 years if they work or study, and 30 years if they do not.
Mahmood said: "Our changes ensure those who are net contributors are encouraged to come to this country and stay here."
She added: "As a result, the Department for Work and Pensions estimates that our reforms will reduce the benefits bill by billions of pounds."
The original version of the plans announced by Mahmood last year would have delayed 799,000 people from gaining permanent residency. Under the updated plans announced on Monday, that number would drop to 517,000.
One of those affected was Ashfak Juned, a Bangladeshi chef working in Birmingham, who told the BBC he was "crying" when he heard his wait for settled status would now last until 2033.
The home secretary also confirmed a number of groups would see their settlement path remain as it is today - including Hong Kong British nationals overseas, armed forces members, people with a British connection and those on legacy routes including the Windrush scheme.
The Refugee Council's Imran Hussain said the plans for those who had travelled to the UK illegally or by small boat and do not work or study to wait 30 years for ILR were "unfair and unworkable".
"The fairest reforms would be making fast and good quality asylum decisions, with those refugees granted protection being helped to rebuild their lives and to contribute, and those with no right to remain helped to leave with dignity," he said.
For the Conservatives, shadow home secretary Chris Philp said opposition from Mahmood's fellow ministers and the "Labour open borders left" had resulted in the changes from Mahmood's original proposals, adding that she was "no longer running the government's immigration policy".
He highlighted figures from March in which Home Office calculations suggested 196,000 care workers and their adult dependants could settle between 2026 and 2030, at an estimated lifetime cost of £9.5bn to taxpayers.
Philp said this was the "cost of today's U-turn".
But Father of the House Sir Edward Leigh, the longest-serving male MP in the Commons, criticised his Conservative colleague for overseeing the so-called Boriswave after Brexit, where net migration peaked at nearly one million in 2023.
"Some of us don't have amnesia," he said.
Liberal Democrat home affairs spokesman Max Wilkinson said the government's reforms were "unravelling".
He added: "Viewing immigration simply as a matter of raw numbers and images of small boat arrivals is degrading this nation's ability to have the informed national discussion that we need."
Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said Mahmood had "shown her true colours".
"She talked a big game on immigration but has u-turned at the first sign of trouble from her left wing Labour colleagues," he said.
Pointing to Home Office estimates that more than 200,000 immigrants arriving on Health and Care visas would be eligible for British citizenship before the next election, he claimed this would cost the taxpayer £50bn over their lifetimes.
He vowed to review citizenship of all those arriving on care visas from today and extend the qualifying period for citizenship to a minimum of 10 years.
Green Party MP Siân Berry said Mahmood had provided a "new obstacle course of hoops and barriers" for migrants living in the UK.
On Monday, the Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) think tank said that skilled workers and their dependants due to settle in the UK under current rules are expected to make a net lifetime contribution of around £115bn through the taxes they pay.

items.title: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
items.description: The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C.
items.content:
Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
- Published
Dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries have been hit by a cyber-attack affecting their refrigerators and freezers.
Around 40 Delhaize supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland.
Sabcobel, a Belgian company that manufactures some of the affected refrigerators, said the units' evaporators were switched to defrost mode, causing them to warm up, in what is believed to be the same method used in last month's incident that hit hundreds of French supermarkets.
Millions of euros worth of food had to be thrown away in October, local media reported at the time.
Stephan Moelans, the CEO of Sabcobel, which operates Delhaize's systems, on Monday told the Belga news agency that the incident was a cyber-attack and that the company had been "working all night and morning to disconnect the affected units from the network".
He said since the French attack in early October, the company had been working to "protect our customers fridges against this vulnerability" but that the units needed physical modifications, not just software updates.
Most supermarkets across Europe are linked to the internet, and maintenance and troubleshooting can be done remotely.
"The simplest solution is to manage the fridges over a secure internet connection. Most of our customers switched to that after the attack in France," Moelans added.
The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C (122F).
It is unclear who is behind the latest apparent attack.
In the US, authorities are investigating what caused refrigeration malfunctions at a number of American military bases in August and working together with French officials to examine whether the incidents could be linked.
Both Belgium and Sweden's national cyber-security agencies said they were monitoring the incident.
The UK's National Cyber Security Centre said it was working with international partners and industry to "fully understand details of an incident". No incidents have been reported in the UK.
In Flanders, northern Belgium, a Delhaize branch in Hoeilaart told news website Het Laatste Nieuws it had lost €100,000 (£83,500) worth of produce.
The manager said that estimate did not even take into account further losses that would result from closing the shop.
Carrefour, a French-owned supermarket, said the incident had only affected 15 of its Belgian stores, adding that measures had been taken immediately to ensure all shops remained open.
A spokesperson for Colruyt Group, which operates Spar stores in Belgium under a franchise system, told Reuters news agency five shops had their fridge systems attacked.
Sweden's budget furniture retailer Ikea said refrigeration systems of its store in the western Belgian city of Mons were affected, with a spokesman quoted by Reuters as saying "we cannot rule out that additional locations may be affected".
In Sweden, several ICA and Coop shops were hit.
A spokesperson for ICA confirmed the incident had affected a "small number of ICA stores operating outside ICA's central network".
"ICA is currently supporting the affected stores in managing the situation," they said.
One of the ICA branches located in Sjöbo, southern Sweden, wrote on social media: "Our refrigerators and freezers have been hacked overnight and they have set the temperature to 50 degrees."
The store was closed earlier but has now reopened to customers.
Seven out of the 800 Coop stores in Sweden were also affected but the "situation is currently contained and under control", the company told the BBC.
In neighbouring Finland, refrigerator malfunctions were detected in some K-stores.
The owner of the supermarket chain Kesko was quoted by Finland's Helsingin Sanomat newspaper as saying its security experts were investigating what caused the problem.
The attack is also affecting shops in Ireland, the Netherlands and Estonia.
In Ireland, it impacted 13 SuperValu supermarkets. A spokesman for the owner of the chain, Musgrave Group, confirmed to The Irish Times that a "cyber incident" affected its refrigeration systems, but added that the impact was limited to a "specific model" of refrigerator.
A spokesperson for Danish manufacturer Danfoss told Dutch public radio channel NOS that the freezing and cooling systems of at least 17 companies in the Netherlands were attacked overnight, affecting butcher shops and small neighbourhood stores.
A Selver supermarket in Estonia was also affected and there are reports of other affected companies in the country, according to ERR.

items.title: 'All this food is now useless': Piles of rubbish after shop freezers hit by cyber-attack
items.description: Dozens of supermarkets in seven European countries dumped huge quantities of food after refrigerators and freezers were targeted in a cyber-attack.
items.content:
'All this food is now useless': Piles of rubbish after shop freezers hit by cyber-attack
In dozens of supermarkets across several European countries, a huge amount of food has been dumped after refrigerators and freezers were targeted in a cyber-attack.
Belgium and Luxemburg saw some of the worst damage, with 40 Delhaize supermarkets affected, and incidents also took place in stores across Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland.
In a branch of supermarket Delhaize in Hoeilaart, just outside the Belgian capital Brussels, the BBC's Europe correspondent Nick Beake found frozen pizzas and ice cream among a mountain of food having to be scrapped. This branch estimated the cost of the damage running to more than €100,000 (£83,500).

items.title: Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
items.description: Officials say at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit a southern Ukrainian village in what the president called an "utterly horrific" attack.
items.content:
Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
- Published
At least 26 people were killed after Russian bombs hit an aid distribution centre, in an attack that Ukraine's leader has called "utterly horrific".
Five people were injured and 27 initially reported missing after at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit the village of Komyshuvakha in the southern Zaporizhzhia region, regional head Mykhailo Semikin said.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said that after the first strike on the local school "used for humanitarian needs", there was a second attack on the place where people were sheltering.
He posted a video showing a huge crater left after Monday's attack, and rescuer teams searching through the rubble.
The Russian military has not publicly commented.
Zelensky initially put the death toll at 18, but Ukraine's state emergencies service DSNS later said 24 people, including two rescuers and four police officers, were confirmed to have been killed.
In his video address late on Monday, Zelensky said 26 people were now known to have died.
He earlier said that "the Russians could not have been unaware that the local residents who remained in Komyshuvakha received humanitarian aid there every week" on Monday.
"This is yet another proof that Russia does not want any de-escalation."
He said that after a recent successful joint Russian-Ukrainian operation to evacuate civilians from the Russia-occupied southern city of Oleshky during a temporary ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, "there was a moment when the next steps could show that peace is possible".
"With such killings, Russia is sending the exact opposite signal - Russia is counting on further killings," Zelensky said.
Meanwhile, Semikin described the Russian attack as a "terrible tragedy" for the village, confirming that "people are still under the rubble".
He said rescue teams were working at the scene, but they had been forced to halt their operation a number of times because of Russian drone attacks in the area.
A day of mourning has been declared for Tuesday across the entire Zaporizhzhia region.
Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Teams from Ukraine, Russia and the US are due to resume peace talks in the next few days after negotiations were suspended in February, with Moscow stepping up attacks as Kyiv virtually ran out of Western-supplied interceptors to defend against missiles.
However, no major breakthrough is expected at the talks that are likely to be held in Abu Dhabi, the United Arab Emirates.

items.title: Copilot in deadly Florida jet crash identified in reports as 20-year-old
items.description: In air traffic audio, a crew member can be heard shouting: "We are going to crash into the ground!"
items.content:
Copilot in deadly Florida jet crash identified in reports as 20-year-old
- Published
A 20-year-old copilot was among nine people killed when a small jet crashed and exploded in Florida on Sunday, according to US media.
Nathalia Filgueiras, who earned her pilot's licence when she was 17, is reported to have been one of two crew members aboard the Learjet 60 from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas when it crashed near West Palm Beach.
The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said it would investigate to what extent ice and turbulence may have contributed to the crash, and whether human error played a role.
One man on the ground sustained a leg injury when the aircraft nosedived on to a street near Cresthaven, nine miles (14 km) from President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago resort.
Images from the scene show a large fiery crater in the middle of a residential suburban street.
The debris was scattered across sports fields, businesses and homes in the area, officials told a news conference on Monday, possible evidence that the plane broke up before it hit the ground.
The NTSB confirmed that after the jet took off from Austin, the crew transmitted to air traffic control that they were encountering ice and moderate turbulence.
"We are picking up precipitation, requesting to climb to 37,000 feet if able," the crew said.
NTSB member Tom Chapman said that less than 30 seconds later, the plane began to descend and the crew issued a mayday call.
The transmission then became "unintelligible", he said, adding that: "Sadly, all aboard were lost."
Flight analysis indicates the jet was plummeting hundreds of feet per second before crashing.
In air traffic control audio, a crew member can be heard declaring an emergency, shouting "we are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000ft per minute", before saying, "we are going to crash into the ground".
About 35 seconds after the initial mayday announcement, the last remark from the cockpit appears to be "we're out of time".
Filgueiras's mother, Camila Corteleti, confirmed to US media that her daughter had died in the fireball.
Corteleti told the New York Times: "She loved the freedom. It was completely different seeing the world from the top."
In a 2023 interview with a local news affiliate of CBS News, Filgueiras spoke proudly of receiving her pilot's licence while still a senior in high school.
"I like being different than everyone," she said. "Some people think that it's weird that I can fly planes, but I can't drive a car, I mean I can but, a lot of people think it's funny."
None of the other eight people on board has been identified.
The NTSB said that ice and turbulence were factors in the crash.
Officials are also trying to find out whether a cockpit voice recorder was on board at the time of the crash and if it can be recovered.
The NTSB said determining the probable cause of the crash will be a "lengthy investigatory process".
As part of the investigation, the NTSB is working with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), representatives from Learjet as well as meteorologists and air traffic control experts.
Recovering the wreckage from the crater on the roadway will be a "daunting challenge", said Timothy Monville, an air safety investigator with the NTSB.
He added that an individual who was in a vehicle near the crash site sustained a leg injury.
Unverified footage posted on social media shows what appears to be a dash-camera recording of the moment of the crash.
"When you see that video, it's a jarring thing," Florida Governor Ron DeSantis told reporters at a news conference on Sunday. "It's like a missile coming down, and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere."
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy described the crash as a "horrific tragedy".
The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office said the crash happened on Military Trail, a six-lane road lined with businesses and restaurants.
Thunderstorms had been reported in the area at the time of the crash.
Trump was at Mar-a-Lago on Sunday morning, and departed from an airport nearby on Air Force One about an hour before the crash.

items.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
items.content:
Watch Trump arrive in New York for his arraignment
1:18
What we covered here
Former President Donald Trump arrived in New York City Monday, a day before he is expected to turn himself in to law enforcement and face more than 30 criminal charges in a Manhattan court following last week’s historic grand jury indictment.
Trump’s legal team said the former president will voluntarily surrender and will look to challenge “every potential issue” once the indictment is unsealed.
Trump, who has vowed to continue his 2024 bid, is the first current or former president in US history who has faced criminal charges. The district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential election.
Trump arraignment has "unparalleled public interest," but it won't be broadcast, judge says
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan wrote his Monday night order that the media’s request to broadcast the arraignment of former President Donald Trump was understandable, but that the news organizations’ interests in providing the broadest possible access to the proceedings must be weighed against “competing interests.”
In rejecting the request to broadcast the arraignment live on television, Merchan still wrote about the historical significance of the proceeding in stark terms.

Judge will only briefly allow photos in the courtroom before Trump arraignment begins
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.
However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”
Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.
The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”
The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.
The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.
Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.
Link Copied!
Tuesday is the first test for Trump to navigate a legal and political strategy
From CNN's Jeff Zeleny
Donald Trump is not planning to speak publicly in New York on Tuesday, aides say, if he follows advice from members of his legal team who have urged the former President to refrain from the vitriol he’s been directing toward the prosecutor and judge presiding over the case.
But that restraint does not extend to Florida, aides said, where he is planning to deliver a full-throated defense of his New York case as well as other investigations he is facing during a prime time address from Mar-a-Lago on Tuesday night.
It’s the first test to see whether Trump can navigate two vasty different approaches to his legal case and his political campaign, which are now inextricably linked.

Trump is "ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow," attorney says
From CNN's Mary Kay Mallonee
Alina Habba, lawyer for former President Donald Trump, gives an interview outside of Trump Tower on March 21 in New York City.
(Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
Alina Habba, who represents Donald Trump in several civil matters, spent time with the former president in New York today and said, “He’s in good spirits. Honestly, he’s as he normally would be. He’s ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow.”
Habba — appearing on on Fox News’ “Jesse Watters” — was asked about the “game plan” for Trump’s appearance in court in Manhattan Tuesday and said, “It’s all mapped out.”
She added, “Barring any surprises, I think that it should be smooth. We’re trying to coordinate and cooperate with everybody to make sure that there are no problems.”
On whether Trump can get a fair trial in Manhattan, Habba said, “No, no. I think it’s very difficult. I’d like to have faith in this state, but I’ve been practicing for him now for a couple years and gone to court in New York for a few years, and I can tell you, it’s not the same as representing anybody else.”

The former president met with attorneys at Trump Tower on the eve of his arraignment
From CNN's Kristen Holmes
From left to right: Susan Necheles, Todd Blanche and Joe Tacopina.
(Reuters/Getty Images)
Former President Donald Trump met with his attorneys Susan Necheles and Joe Tacopina at Trump Tower after arriving in New York City Monday, a source familiar with the meeting told CNN.
It is unclear if the newest addition to Trump’s New York legal team, Todd Blanche, attended the meeting.
Trump is expected to be arraigned Tuesday.

Photos: Trump arrives in New York City a day before his expected arraignment
From CNN's Photo Desk
Former President Donald Trump has landed in New York’s La Guardia Airport ahead of his expected Tuesday arraignment in a Manhattan courthouse.
History was made Thursday when he was indicted by a New York grand jury. It’s the first time that a current or former US president has been criminally charged.
The Manhattan district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme and cover-up involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential campaign.
Trump’s attorney said he plans to file “substantial” legal challenges. The former president has repeatedly denied wrongdoing in the matter and accused Democrats of targeting him politically.

Former president poised to huddle with advisers at Trump Tower

A supporter of former President Donald Trump holds a "Trump Won" sign outside of Trump Tower in New York on Monday, April 3.
(Alex Kent/Bloomberg/Getty Images)
A small group of supporters chanted as former President Donald Trump arrived at his namesake tower on Monday afternoon, with a handful of people waving banners with messages like “Trump won” and “Arrest Biden.”
While Trump couldn’t see his admirers as he entered a side door on 56th Street, his arrival came with more fanfare and security than at any other time in his post presidency.
Now that he is inside the building — where he launched his presidential bid nearly eight years ago — Trump is expected to meet with lawyers and political advisers on the eve of his arraignment, an aide told CNN.
Trump’s mood was described by an adviser as “defiant and focused,” as he watched expansive television coverage while flying back to his native New York City from Florida.

Special counsel has secured evidence of how Trump handled classified records at Mar-a-Lago, sources say
From CNN's Katelyn Polantz and Evan Perez
Special counsel prosecutors have secured evidence including daily notes, texts, emails and photographs and are focused on cataloging how Donald Trump handled classified records around the Mar-a-Lago resort and those who may have witnessed the former president with them, according to multiple sources familiar with the investigation.
The new details come amid signs the Justice Department is taking steps that are typically near the end of an investigation.
The recent investigative activity before a federal grand jury in Washington, DC, also includes subpoenaing witnesses in March and April who had previously spoken to investigators, the sources said. While the FBI interviewed many aides and workers at Mar-a-Lago nearly a year ago voluntarily, grand jury appearances are transcribed and under oath — an indication the prosecutors are locking in witness testimony.
The focus of both the mishandling of records and obstruction of justice probes has remained on the actions of the former president, the sources say. That includes prosecutors pursuing evidence of Trump’s intent to keep classified records after he left the White House, plus his knowledge that the records remained in his possession after the Justice Department demanded their return last May.
